VERDICT: CLEAN
BOUNDARY: Verified that both spaces are non‑empty (P a singleton, ℝ the real line) and carry their intended topologies (the unique topology on a point and the standard topology on ℝ). No bijection exists from a finite set to an uncountable set, so no homeomorphism can exist regardless of topology; the definition of homeomorphism requires a bijection. The maps i and q are continuous by trivial pre‑image checks. The homotopy H(x,t)=(1−t)x (from the cited contractibility example) is continuous and provides i∘q = c₀ ≃ id_ℝ, while q∘i = id_P exactly. These data satisfy the definition of homotopy equivalence. No degenerate, empty, zero, one, endpoint, or choice issues are present; no biconditional is claimed. No counterexample to the statement exists.
SOURCES: Inspected all five cited items: def‑homeomorphism‑and‑open‑maps, def‑homotopy‑equivalence, ex‑intervals‑and‑euclidean‑spaces‑are‑contractible, fs‑homotopy‑equivalent‑spaces‑are‑homeomorphic, thm‑r‑uncountable. Their full text (as supplied) confirms that each citation accurately supports the claim it is used for.
